title: Expert public profile (/{username})
summary: The profile's booking mechanics are sound: real next times, a sticky card on desktop, a sticky bar on phones, a cancellation line on every service. What is weak is the person. With no photo, no profession line and a short bio, the page is a monogram, a name and grey small print, and the one fact Eleva has checked (the professional registration) reads like a legal footnote. The change that matters most is to turn that checked registration into a visible proof block beside the name and to give every profile a structured "about" (profession, focus, approach, training, what a first session looks like) that still looks complete when an expert is new.
strengths: Next open times are on the profile itself, grouped by day, with the member's timezone named. On desktop the booking card stays in view while she reads (01-profile-paid.desktop.jpg).
Phones already have a sticky bar with the starting price and "See times" (01-profile-paid.mobile.jpg, 02-profile-free.mobile.jpg). Keep it and make it do more.
The registration line is real, checkable proof: the professional body links to its public register and the licence number is shown. Few marketplaces offer this. It needs presence, not replacement.
Every service states its cancellation window in plain words ("Free cancellation up to 24 hours before"), and the booking card closes with "No account needed".
"How I can help" and "About me" are in the expert's own voice, which suits a page about a person.
The FAQ asks the right questions ("Who provides my care?", "What does Eleva check?") and answers them honestly.

The source already supports a large portrait hero, area-of-care links above the name, a credential line and a "Training and credentials" timeline. They are simply empty for a new expert, so the design problem is the fallback, not the full state.

findings.title: The checked registration reads as small print
findings.detail: "Ordem dos Fisioterapeutas · Licence no. 9115 · ERS registration no. 182844" is one line of 14px grey text between the facts and the share button. Nothing says Eleva checked it, when, or what the numbers mean. "ERS" is unexplained and the body's name is in Portuguese on an English page. The explanation exists, but as the sixth closed item of the FAQ at the bottom ("What does Eleva check?"). A member deciding whether to trust this person with her health has no visible signal that anyone verified anything.
findings.recommendation: Make it a proof block directly under the name: a check icon, "Registration checked by Eleva" with the month it was checked, then the body in plain words ("Registered physiotherapist, Ordem dos Fisioterapeutas, no. 9115") with "View on the public register", and the health regulator registration on its own line with its name written out. Add a small "What we check" link that opens one honest paragraph: Eleva checks the professional registration before a profile goes live; experts describe their own training and experience. Put the same check mark beside the name on the explorer card.

findings.title: There is little proof of the person beyond a name
findings.detail: With a two-sentence bio the profile has no years in practice, no focus areas, no approach, no training, no description of a first session and no voice from other members. "About me" sits below every service card, and on phones below the booking card too, about 2,100px down. "What to expect" exists only as a closed accordion inside one service. The free profile has no "About me" at all, so the page goes from one service straight to a booking FAQ. The source has a "Training and credentials" timeline, but an expert who skips it leaves nothing behind.
findings.recommendation: Give the profile a fixed spine that expert setup fills step by step: (1) an at-a-glance row under the header (profession, years in practice, focus areas); (2) "My approach", three or four sentences prompted in setup; (3) "Your first session", three numbered steps the expert edits from a default for her profession; (4) "Training and credentials"; (5) "What members say", shown once an expert has a few reviews from members who completed a session, and a quiet "New on Eleva" tag until then rather than empty stars. Move a two-line version of the bio into the header so it is read before the prices. Ask for approach and at least one training entry before a profile can be published.

findings.title: Without a photo the header loses the person
findings.detail: The header pairs a 110px monogram circle with a 60px serif name. The monogram looks like an account avatar from a dashboard, not someone you would book. The source shows a 4:5 portrait as the largest element when a photo exists, so a profile with and without one are two different pages, and new experts get the weaker one. Nothing under the name says what she is: the only hint of a profession is the name of the regulatory body in the small print.
findings.recommendation: Ask for a portrait before a profile can be published, with a short guide in setup (face, daylight, plain background) and a crop tool. Add a profession line as the first thing under the name ("Physiotherapist · Pelvic health"), required, taken from the areas of care. For the rare profile still without a photo, keep the full-size 4:5 frame with a branded Eleva illustration and the initials, so the layout and the page's weight stay the same.

findings.title: Header facts run together as one grey sentence
findings.detail: Languages, how you meet, cities and countries served are joined with dots into one paragraph of small grey text. On the free profile the country list names 27 countries and runs four lines on desktop and six on a phone, pushing the first service to about 720px on mobile, below the first screen. The facts a member scans for first (does she speak my language, can I see her in my city) are the hardest to pick out.
findings.recommendation: Break the facts into three short rows with icons: languages, how you meet ("Video, phone" or "Video, in person in Lisboa, Porto and Madrid"), and where members can be. Collapse long country lists ("Members across the EU", with the list behind "See countries"). On phones keep the whole header within one screen so the first service or the first times are visible without scrolling.

findings.title: On a phone the times sit under every service, and the sticky bar only scrolls
findings.detail: The mobile order is header, service cards, then the booking card. On the paid profile the booking card starts about 1,450px down with two services; an expert with five services pushes it far further. The sticky bar helps, but it shows only "From €45.00" and "See times", the same label as the button in each service card, and it jumps down the page instead of starting a booking. A member never sees when the expert is next free until she gets there.
findings.recommendation: Show the next open time in the header on phones ("Next: Mon 16 Nov, 08:00") and in the sticky bar beside the price. Rename the bar's button "Book a session" and open a bottom sheet with the same picker (service, how you meet, day, time), so booking starts from anywhere on the page. Add a short row of anchor tabs under the header (Services, About, Training, Reviews) so the long page can be jumped through.

findings.title: The availability card packs place and mode into the time chip
findings.detail: For an expert with three locations the first day shows "08:00 Madrid, 12:00 Lisboa, 12:00 Porto, 12:00 Madrid, 12:30 Lisboa, 12:30 Porto". The same hour appears three times and the city, the bigger decision, is the smallest text in the chip. On the free profile each time appears twice, told apart only by a small video or phone icon with no label. Only one day and six times are shown, and the way to other days is a text link.
findings.recommendation: Ask in order: service, then how and where (a segmented choice: Video, Lisboa, Porto, Madrid), then a strip of the next seven days with unavailable days greyed, then the times for the chosen day. Label modes in words. Keep the summary lines at the foot of the card (length and price, "No account needed", cancellation window); they are good.

findings.title: Service cards are uneven and repeat the same action
findings.detail: "Follow-up" comes before "First visit", so a new member reads the wrong service first. Follow-up has addresses, an included item and two accordions; First visit has a title, a price and nothing else. The eyebrow "45-MIN IN PERSON · LISBOA, PORTO, MADRID" is repeated by three address rows directly under it, and on phones it wraps to three lines of spaced capitals beside the price. Each card has its own "See times" button, the booking card has "See all times" and the phone has a sticky "See times": three controls with nearly the same label and different behaviour. Prices carry cents ("€45.00").
findings.recommendation: Order services with first visits first and tag one "Start here". Require a one-sentence description per service and show it on the card. Use one meta line in sentence case with icons ("45 min · In person · Lisboa, Porto, Madrid") and keep full addresses behind "See addresses". Make the card's button "Choose a time", which selects that service in the booking card (or opens the sheet on phones). Show whole euros.

findings.title: The empty profile is a dead end
findings.detail: A profile with no services shows "Patricia Mota isn't taking bookings here yet. See their work below." Below there is a one-line bio and a six-question FAQ about booking, which does not apply. The headline above says "Available for consultations on Eleva.", which contradicts the notice. The right-hand column is empty and the member is offered nothing to do next.
findings.recommendation: Replace the notice with a proper state in the booking column: "[Name] is setting up on Eleva", a "Tell me when bookings open" email field, and two or three experts in the same area who can be booked now. Hide the booking FAQ on this state and keep the proof block and About. Remove the default headline; show the profession line instead. Best of all, hold publication until one service is live.

findings.title: Reassurance is locked in a closed FAQ at the bottom
findings.detail: "Booking with Eleva" is six closed accordions after everything else. The answers a hesitant member needs before she books (how payment works, that she needs no account, how she joins, who provides the care, what Eleva checked) are all one tap away and none are visible. A first-time visitor who has never heard of Eleva sees no statement of what Eleva is doing for her on this page.
findings.recommendation: Keep the FAQ, and lift three points into a visible strip near the booking card: "Registration checked by Eleva", "Pay securely, cancel free up to 24 hours before", "Join from your email, no app or account". Add a short "How it works" row of three steps above the FAQ: choose a time, pay securely, join from your confirmation email.

findings.title: Wording details
findings.detail: "Times in Lisbon time" repeats itself. "45 min · from €45.00 total" joins "from" and "total", which pull in opposite directions. "ERS registration no." assumes the member knows the regulator. "See their work below" points at content that is not there. "Share this page" has the same visual weight as the only link to the expert's own website. No Mobbin reference was needed for these; they are copy fixes.
findings.recommendation: "Times shown in Lisbon time" or "Lisbon time (WET)". "45 min · from €45". "Health regulator (ERS) registration". On the empty state, name what is there ("Read more about Patricia below") or drop the sentence. Reduce share to an icon button with a label for screen readers.

references.pattern: Identity, then booking, in the first screen
references.why: The first phone screen holds a round photo, a badge with an info icon, name with credential, specialty, rating and review count, then "Book an appointment" at once: a location selector ("2 more locations with availability soon") and tomorrow's times as a grid of large buttons with "more". Place is chosen before time, so each time appears once.
references.apply: On phones put the profession under the name and the next times directly after the header. Choose location or mode first, then show times, so the chips carry only the hour.

references.pattern: No availability: say why, offer "Notify me"
references.why: Where the times would be, a grey panel titled "No upcoming availability" explains in two lines, and a full-width "Notify me" button sits under it. The location selector above still notes "3 more locations with availability soon". The booking section keeps its place and its heading.
references.apply: The empty profile and the "next two weeks are full" state: keep the booking block, explain in one sentence, and offer "Tell me when bookings open".
references.query: booking app provider profile with no available appointments

references.why: One section, four fixed labels: Professional statement (two lines and "Read more"), Education as a short list of school and degree, Practice names, then languages further down. Each label is always in the same place, so a member can find training on any profile.
references.apply: A fixed "Training and credentials" block with the same sub-labels on every profile, each trimmed to two or three lines with "Read more".

references.why: Tapping the info icon on the badge beside the name opens a small sheet titled "What is this?" with one sentence on what the badge means and a Close button. The claim and its meaning are one tap apart.
references.apply: A "Registration checked by Eleva" mark beside the name that opens one plain sentence on what Eleva checked.

references.pattern: Platform vetting statement, "Things to know", sticky price and Reserve
references.why: The left column stays fixed: photo, service title, one-line description, rating, and at its foot "From $31 / guest" with a Reserve button. The right column scrolls through "Things to know" (guest requirements, accessibility, cancellation policy as three icon items) and a panel with a seal: "Estheticians on Airbnb are vetted for quality", one sentence on what is evaluated, and "Learn more". Travel marketplace, kept for how the platform states its own checks on a provider's page.
references.apply: A visible panel on every profile saying what Eleva checks, in one sentence with a link, and a three-item "Good to know" row (cancellation, how you join, no account needed) in place of a closed FAQ.

references.pattern: Stat card and icon facts with "Identity verified"
references.why: A card holds the portrait, name and three numbers (reviews, rating, years hosting). Beside it "About" lists facts one per row, each with an icon: work, languages spoken, where the person lives, and "Identity verified" as an underlined link. The bio follows, then a row of review cards. Travel marketplace, kept for the header structure.
references.apply: Header facts as icon rows, with verification as its own linked row, and a small stat card (years in practice, sessions on Eleva once there are some).
references.query: service marketplace listing page with host qualifications

references.pattern: A dated check in its own "Safety" block
references.why: A "Safety" card opens with a line linking to the Safety Center, then a row with a shield icon: "Care.com Background Check, Completed 07/31/25" and a green tick. The check is named, dated and attributed to the platform. A sticky bar at the top keeps the caregiver's name and a Contact button in view. Care marketplace; the paid upsell rows below the first one are not what Eleva takes.
references.apply: The proof block: who checked, what, when, with a link to the explanation, and the register number beside it.
references.query: caregiver marketplace profile page with background check badge and reviews

references.pattern: Reviews with a summary, beside a sticky booking panel
references.why: "What my students say" opens with the score, "Based on 50 student reviews" and a one-line summary, then review cards with name, date and "Show more". The panel on the right stays in view: rating, lessons taught and price in one row, the primary booking button, secondary actions, and two lines of activity ("Popular", "Usually responds in 4 hrs"). Education marketplace, kept for the structure.
references.apply: A "What members say" section tied to completed sessions, and a line or two of live proof in the booking card ("Usually confirms within a day").
references.query: caregiver marketplace profile page with background check badge and reviews

references.pattern: Anchor tabs, stats, chips and a full-width sticky "Book now"
references.why: A professional's profile on a phone. Tabs under the name (Profile, Services, Portfolio, Reviews with a count) jump down the page. Two stats (appointments completed, clients served), then interests and languages as chips. Each service row has a small "Book" button, and a full-width "Book now" bar stays at the bottom. Beauty and wellness marketplace, kept for the mobile structure.
references.apply: Anchor tabs on phones, languages and focus as chips, a small per-service button that feeds one sticky "Book a session" action.

references.pattern: Day strip with unavailable days, times below, summary beside
references.why: A strip of seven days with the chosen day filled and unavailable days struck through, a column of times under it, and on the right a summary card that updates (place, date, time, service, total) with Continue. Who you are booking with is a small selector above the dates. Beauty and wellness marketplace, kept for the picker.
references.apply: In the booking card: a seven-day strip instead of a single day, with the how-and-where choice above it and the running summary Eleva already has below.
references.query: doctor profile page with available appointment times

references.pattern: "Here's how you and your provider will work together"
references.why: A portrait with a credential tag, then three numbered steps, each a bold label and one sentence, describing what the provider will do and in what order. It is short enough to read in ten seconds. Telehealth product; a step in a flow rather than a profile, kept for the content pattern.
references.apply: "Your first session" on every profile: three numbered steps in the expert's words, from a default per profession.

references.pattern: A new profile that still looks complete
references.why: A profile with no history: photo, name, city and join date, then a "Verified info" list where each item has its own tick, then languages and work. The About text sits on the right with "More", and the reviews area keeps its place with a quiet one-line note. The page is sparse but ordered, because every block has a label and a fixed position. Car sharing marketplace, kept for the new-profile state.
references.apply: A new expert's page keeps every section in place with short content. Eleva frames it as "New on Eleva" and lets the checked registration carry the trust until reviews exist.
references.query: caregiver marketplace profile page with background check badge and reviews

judging_criteria: Is the checked registration a visible block beside the name that says who checked, what and when, with a one-tap explanation? (03-profile/07, 03-profile/04)
Does the first phone screen show who she is (photo, name, profession) and when she is next free? (03-profile/01)
Can a member start booking from anywhere on a phone through one sticky action that opens the picker? (03-profile/09, 03-profile/05)
Does each time appear once, with service and how or where chosen before the time, across a strip of days? (03-profile/01, 03-profile/10)
Does the profile have fixed, labelled sections for approach, training and a three-step first session, in the same place on every profile? (03-profile/03, 03-profile/11)
Does a new expert's page (no reviews, short bio) still look complete and ordered? (03-profile/12, 03-profile/06)
When an expert cannot be booked, does the booking block explain why and offer a next step? (03-profile/02)
